problem_motivation.content: Chiral anomaly is difficult to identify because it can be confused with weak localization
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Since chiral anomaly is not easy to identify and may be confused with the weak localization, long established in the literature8, we perform additional tests to verify these mechanisms.

problem_motivation.content: Obtaining a supercell configuration that actually contains Weyl points is difficult because calculations usually give positive or negative gaps.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Usually we obtain results with positive or negative energy gaps. That is why finding the system containing Weyl points is not an easy task.

prior_approach.content: Theory predicted that chemical disorder affects the multivalley electron system and positions the Fermi level near Weyl nodes, identified by DFT.
prior_approach.evidence_span: We experimentally verify the theoretically pre- dicted role of chemical disorder in this multivalley electron system, which leads to sequential band inversions in various valleys and places the Fermi level close to the pairs of Weyl nodes, as identified in the density functional theory calculations.

prior_approach.content: Liang et al. used pressure in Pb1−xSnxTe:In to induce a transition to a topological metallic phase associated with Weyl nodes.
prior_approach.evidence_span: For instance Liang et al. demonstrate that applying pressure to Pb1–xSnxTe:In, material undergoes a pressure-driven transition from TCI to a topological metallic phase associated with Weyl nodes.

prior_approach.content: The conventional treatment uses the virtual crystal approximation to describe the composition-driven trivial-to-topological transition.
prior_approach.evidence_span: According to the classical convention, these materials are usually considered within the virtual crystal approximation (VCA), where, for a given composition, the transition from trivial to topological phase occurs.

prior_approach.content: Recent work by Wang et al. showed that chemical disorder in Pb1−xSnxSe can induce an intermediate WSM phase via sequential band inversion.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Wang et al.13 demonstrated that chemical disorder on cation position in Pb1–xSnxSe alloys can induce an intermediate WSM phase during the sequential band inversion in four ”L” valleys.

prior_approach.content: Earlier work by Lusakowski et al. on Pb1−xSnxTe found that alloy disorder broadens the transition region and creates an extended nontrivial regime.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Similar conclusion was reached earlier by Lusakowski et al.12 in the study on Pb1–xSnxTe alloys. In particular, the work shows how alloy disorder broadens the transition region between trivial and topological phases, producing an extended transition regime associated with nontrivial topology.

prior_approach.content: Earlier publications reported chiral-anomaly-induced negative longitudinal magnetoresistance in Bi1−xSbx and other Dirac/Weyl semimetals.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Chiral anomaly-induced negative MR∥has been observed for the first time in Bi1–xSbx, x = 0.03 in 201319. Soon after, researchers also reported its presence for Dirac and Weyl semimetals such as: Cd3As222,23 , NaBi324 , TaAs6,25,26, TaP28, α-Sn29 .

prior_approach.content: Argyres and Adams modeled longitudinal magnetoresistance, while Abrikosov's quantum magnetoresistance model predicted non-saturating linear transverse magnetoresistance.
prior_approach.evidence_span: These findings were made independently by two research groups - the model of Argyres and Adams6,30 addresses longitudinal magnetoresistance and may lead to negative MR∥, whereas second model of quantum magnetoresistance, implemented by Abrikosov31,32, predicts a non-saturating linear MR⊥.

prior_approach.content: A Princeton group observed a nonlinear Hall contribution in Pb1−xSnxTe and attributed it to large Berry curvature near Weyl nodes.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A few years later3 the scientific group from Princeton observed a nonlinear Hall contribution (σyx) beyond the ordinary linear Hall effect in Pb1–xSnxTe, which they assigned to the large Berry curvature situated near the Weyl nodes.

prior_approach.content: The authors' earlier study analyzed band inversion, band offsets, and Cr resonant levels across the full Pb1−xSnxTe:Cr phase diagram.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Our recent studies were devoted to the band inversion and band-offsets in Cr-doped Pb1–xSnxTe bulk crystals covering whole range of Sn composition (0 ≤x ≤1)42. In that study we also determine the position of the Cr resonant level over the entire Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr phase diagram (0 ≤x ≤1).

prior_approach.content: Previous publications reported characterization details of the crystals using SEM, EDX, XRD, SIMS, and EDXF.
prior_approach.evidence_span: All the details regarding characterization of the obtained crys- tals, including chemical composition, morphology and crystal structure - namely scanning electron microscopy (SEM) together with the energy dispersive X-ray spectrometry (EDX), X-ray diffraction (XRD), secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) and energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (EDXF) - have been reported in our previous publications42,76.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies performed SQUID magnetometry and EPR magnetic measurements.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Also our magnetic measurements, including SQUID magnetometry and Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR), performed during previous studies42,51,76,77

prior_approach.content: Negative magnetoresistance in B∥E geometry is a commonly used signature associated with chiral anomaly in Weyl semimetals.
prior_approach.evidence_span: This geometry was chosen to measure negative magnetoresistance, commonly associated with the chiral anomaly in Weyl semimetals.

prior_approach.content: The need to reduce Pb 6p spin-orbit strength in DFT had been discussed previously.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The necessity of such reduction was previously discussed in Ref. 80.

prior_approach.content: The method used to find Weyl points was taken from an earlier reference.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The method of finding the Weyl points was described in Ref. 47.

prior_approach.content: A standard fitting formula combining chiral-anomaly and weak-antilocalization terms was used.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The above formula consists of two contributions: (i) chiral anomaly propor- tional to B2 term4 and (ii) quantum interference term in the form of the weak antilocalization for the 3D WSM system5,6.

prior_approach.content: An alternative prior interpretation attributes magnetic-field-periodic oscillations to pseudospin Landau levels in the ultra-quantum limit.
prior_approach.evidence_span: There is also another alternative, considering oscillations periodic in the magnetic field, attributed to pseudospin Landau levels in the regime of ultra quantum limit10,11.

prior_limitation.content: Use of the Fermi-level pinning effect had previously been limited to thermoelectric performance improvement.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: whose application has so far been limited solely to improving thermoelectric performance43–46.

rejected_alternative.content: The paper interprets the transition via disorder-driven WSM formation rather than the standard VCA picture with a single inversion point at x = 0.35.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: This behavior may be understood in terms of compositional-disorder driven transition to WSM phase according to earlier theoretical predictions12,13,47, instead of the VCA approach with band inversion point situated at x = 0.35 in Pb1–xSnxTe.

rejected_alternative.content: Magnetic-origin giant/colossal MR is rejected because the effect is angle-selective rather than present in both geometries
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Otherwise, if the observed effect were due to giant or colossal MR of magnetic origin, reported in literature62–64 it should occur in both perpendicular and parallel MR configurations.

rejected_alternative.content: Current-jetting is excluded as the source of negative magnetoresistance
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: We also exclude the geometry and size effects, the so called current-jetting, which can result in negative magneto-resistance, but is associated mainly with inhomogeneities of the electric field distribution6,59,65.

rejected_alternative.content: Alternative explanations for linear MR other than Abrikosov quantum limit are ruled out
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Moreover, we rule out the hypotheses regarding the origin of the linear MR in our samples arising from other reasons than Abrikosov’s quantum limit31,32, mentioned in the Introduction57.

rejected_alternative.content: Parish-Littlewood inhomogeneous two-component conduction is excluded because inclusions are scarce and samples are homogeneous
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: In particular we exclude the conduction through two-component inhomogeneous system, such as PbSe matrix with embedded Ag metallic precipitates - the so called Parish-Littlewood model66,67. As mentioned, the presence of Cr-Te nanoinclusions in our samples is very low and does not contribute to conduction. High compositional homogeneity of our samples is confirmed by the SEM/EDX measurements42. It is also confirmed by very similar resistivities obtained for both pairs of contacts. In this regard, we do not have a system containing multiple precipitates differing significantly in resistance that could affect the results.

rejected_alternative.content: Fermi-arc origin of oscillations is rejected because the samples are far too thick and no such signatures are seen
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: In contrast, thicknesses of our samples are approximately 0.5-1 mm, meaning several orders of magnitude larger. Therefore, based on our data, we do not observe any signatures of Fermi arcs beyond the effects attributed to the chiral anomaly.

rejected_alternative.content: A 2D electron-gas explanation of the oscillations is rejected because oscillations remain finite at 90 degrees
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: The finite oscillation frequency observed at an angle of 90 degrees, provides direct evidence that the oscillations do not originate from a 2D electron gas, since in that case, no oscillations would be expected for the B ∥E configuration.

rejected_alternative.content: Using larger supercells was considered but deemed impractical because the calculations are too time-consuming.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Probably the problem would be partially solved by considering larger supercells, but the calculations are long-lasting and this approach is impractical.

rejected_alternative.content: They reject the pseudospin-Landau-level explanation and instead use the simpler Aharonov-Bohm/Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak interpretation.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: However, we exclude this scenario and adopt the simpler A-B and A-A-S interpretation.

causal_claim.content: Chemical disorder causes sequential band inversions in different valleys and places the Fermi level near pairs of Weyl nodes.
causal_claim.evidence_span: chemical disorder in this multivalley electron system, which leads to sequential band inversions in various valleys and places the Fermi level close to the pairs of Weyl nodes

causal_claim.content: Doping with mixed-valence Cr resonant impurities enables tuning of carrier concentration via dopant resonant states.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Doping with mixed-valence Cr resonant impurities enables exploitation of the unique properties of dopant resonant states, which provide an effective means of tuning carrier concentration.

causal_claim.content: The combination of chemical disorder and Cr resonant doping pins the Fermi level near nodal touching points over a wide composition range.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The combination of these two effects results in the pinning of the Fermi level in the vicinity of the nodal touching points across a wide range of composition.

causal_claim.content: Breaking time-reversal or inversion symmetry can drive materials into Weyl semimetal states through band inversion during a topological phase transition.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a consequence of this symmetry breaking, these materials may evolve into Weyl semimetals through band inversion processes.

causal_claim.content: Applying pressure splits a degenerate Dirac cone into two Weyl cones of opposite chirality separated in momentum space.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This results in splitting one degenerate Dirac cone where opposite-chirality fermions overlap into two nondegenerate Weyl cones of opposite chiralities separated in momentum space.

causal_claim.content: Chemical disorder and other symmetry-breaking effects can alter band inversion by lifting valley degeneracy.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Introducing chemical disorder and other effects, that break local crystal symmetries and split valley degeneracy at high symmetry points of the Brillouin zone (BZ) may lead to significant changes, e.g. in the band inversion process in comparison with TIs/TCIs.

causal_claim.content: Closing the bulk gap removes the Dirac mass term and yields a massless Weyl equation with linear dispersion near Weyl nodes.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The main highlight of this work in our context is that since a bulk energy-gap, responsible for the mass-term of the Dirac equation is closed in WSMs this may be converted into a massless Weyl equation which results in linear energy dispersion in the vicinity of the two Weyl nodes16,17.

causal_claim.content: Spin-momentum locking suppresses spin-independent backscattering and leads to large non-saturating magnetoresistance and very high mobility.
causal_claim.evidence_span: electrons in WSMs have spin locked to the momentum, and thus do not undergo back-scattering by spin-independent processes... As a result, they behave like massles relativistic Dirac fermions, giving rise to large non-saturated magnetoresistance, and hence very high mobilities

causal_claim.content: The nontrivial nature of Weyl fermions causes chiral symmetry to be broken, producing the Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Several decades after Weyl’s achievements, Adler, Bell and Jackiw demonstrated that due to the nontrivial nature of Weyl fermions, the chiral symmetry is no longer preserved, leading to the Adler-Bell-Jackiv anomaly.

causal_claim.content: Applying parallel electric and magnetic fields causes nonconservation of chiral charge between opposite-chirality Weyl nodes.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Chiral anomaly manifests itself as a non-conservation of chiral charge between two Weyl nodes of opposite chiralities when applying parallel electric and magnetic fields (E ∥B) to the material.

causal_claim.content: Both positive linear transverse magnetoresistance and negative longitudinal magnetoresistance may arise from entering the extreme quantum limit.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Interestingly, both mentioned mechanisms - positive linear, non-saturating MR⊥and negative MR∥, may be the consequence of one and the same phenomenon - both may originate from the system entering the extreme quantum limit, i.e. where all electrons occupy only the lowest Landau level.

causal_claim.content: Berry curvature near Weyl nodes strongly affects longitudinal transport and Hall responses.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The Berry curvature associated with Weyl nodes plays a central role in determining the physical properties of these materials, strongly influencing both: longitudinal charge transport, reflected in the chiral anomaly, and Hall responses.

causal_claim.content: Broken inversion symmetry produces an asymmetric Berry curvature distribution in the nonlinear quantum Hall effect.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The resulting asymmetric Berry curvature distribution originates from the broken inversion symmetry under which electrons at momenta k and –k possess opposite Berry curvature.

causal_claim.content: Different occupation of states at k and −k leads to a net Berry curvature.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Hence, charge states for k and -k will be occupied differently leading to the net Berry curvature.

causal_claim.content: Fermi level pinning enabled determination of the Cr resonant level over the full phase diagram.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This is possible due to the Fermi level pinning effect

causal_claim.content: Cooling through the trivial-to-WSM transition freezes out trivial bulk carriers and leaves metallic WSM surface-state carriers
causal_claim.evidence_span: the resistivity of the sample slowly increases as the temperature is lowered starting from RT, since as the sample undergoes the transition from the trivial to the WSM phase, the trivial bulk carriers are gradually ”frozen out” and the metallic carriers, associated with surface states of 3D WSM remain.

causal_claim.content: Low carrier concentration of TCI surface states causes high zero-field resistivity
causal_claim.evidence_span: The zero field resistivity of these states is high since the concentration of the surface-states charge carriers is very low (1016 cm−3).

causal_claim.content: If the effect were magnetic giant/colossal MR, it should appear in both perpendicular and parallel configurations
causal_claim.evidence_span: Otherwise, if the observed effect were due to giant or colossal MR of magnetic origin, reported in literature62–64 it should occur in both perpendicular and parallel MR configurations.

causal_claim.content: Large perpendicular MR hides oscillations unless a second derivative is taken
causal_claim.evidence_span: This is a result of a large magnetoresistance MR⊥and to extract the oscillating component a second derivative of the raw data with respect to 1/B should be taken.

causal_claim.content: Disorder suppresses distinct high-amplitude SdH oscillations typical of high-mobility Weyl fermions
causal_claim.evidence_span: Although quantum transport effects can still be detected, the disorder prevents the emergence of distinct, high amplitude SdH oscillations that are typically associated with high mobility Weyl fermions.

causal_claim.content: Cr doping pins the Fermi level near nodal touching points over a wide Sn range
causal_claim.evidence_span: To investigate these effects, we achieve pinning of the Fermi level in the vicinity of the nodal touching points in Pb1–xSnxTe over a wide range of Sn compositions by doping crystals with Cr.

causal_claim.content: Cr resonant-donor doping pins the Fermi level near the zero-gap state and enables strong topological transport contributions
causal_claim.evidence_span: To reach the physical regime with the sizeable topological contributions to electron transport we successfully applied doping with the resonant donor centre of Cr pinning the Fermi level close to zero-gap state.

causal_claim.content: The small amount of Cr-Te nanoinclusions means they do not affect transport.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Nevertheless, their amount is relatively small and hence they do not affect transport of our samples.

causal_claim.content: Observation of the quantum nonlinear Hall effect provided complementary evidence for nontrivial Berry curvature and supported identifying the Weyl semimetal phase.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Observation of this effect provided complementary evidence for nontrivial Berry curvature and supported the identification of the Weyl semimetal phase in Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr.

causal_claim.content: The mismatch with the two-carrier model implies another mechanism dominates magnetotransport.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This means that a notable mecha- nism dominates the magnetotransport in the current system

causal_claim.content: Small electric/magnetic-field misalignment causes the high-field deviation from the model through added positive magnetoresistance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Deviation of the high-field conductivity from the theoretical model originates from a small admixture of large positive magnetoresistance due to a small misalignment between the electric and magnetic fields.

causal_claim.content: Observation of chiral anomaly in the parallel configuration supports interpreting the system as a 3D Weyl semimetal.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The presence of chiral anomaly in the parallel configuration supports the interpretation that our system is a 3D WSM.

causal_claim.content: If weak-antilocalization to weak-localization crossover were responsible, the effect would appear in both geometries, so it is not the origin here.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Additionally, it is not related to the weak antilocalization – weak localization transition, since if this were the origin of our results, it would be present as well in the parallel and perpendicular configurations.

causal_claim.content: Agreement between DC and AC data confirms chiral anomaly as the source of the observed effects.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The results obtained using both techniques are identical, confirming that the chiral anomaly underlies the observed effects.

causal_claim.content: Agreement between DC and AC data rules out thermoelectric artifacts.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It also excludes thermoelectric effects, such as Peltier or Seebeck effect.

causal_claim.content: Magnetic-field-periodic oscillations arise from interference of electron wavefunctions around enclosed magnetic flux.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The oscillations periodic in the magnetic field arise due to the interference of the amplitudes of the electron wave function as the electron encircles the closed loop surroounding the magnetic flux.

causal_claim.content: Aharonov-Bohm versus Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak paths produce a twofold phase change and therefore h/e versus h/2e flux periods.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This gives the twofold change in the phases of the amplitudes of the A-B and A-A-S oscillations. As a result, the flux period θ in the magnetic field equals h/e or h/2e, respectively.

mechanism_principle.content: Disorder changes a sharp concurrent VCA-like band inversion into a sequential inversion over a finite composition interval where WSM-like states can appear.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: From physical perspective, both studies describe essentially the same mechanism - disorder transforms a sharp and concurrent (VCA-like) band inversion into a sequential one with the finite composition range where WSM-like states may emerge.

mechanism_principle.content: The unusual transport behavior is explained by a compositional-disorder-driven transition to the WSM phase rather than a simple VCA band inversion at x = 0.35.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This behavior may be understood in terms of compositional-disorder driven transition to WSM phase according to earlier theoretical predictions12,13,47, instead of the VCA approach with band inversion point situated at x = 0.35 in Pb1–xSnxTe.

mechanism_principle.content: Small effective mass indicates carriers occupy linearly dispersing bands near Weyl nodes
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The relatively small effective mass obtained in this analysis corresponds to carriers occupying linearly dispersing bands near the Weyl nodes.

mechanism_principle.content: Disorder likely reduces Landau-level separation and increases overlap, enabling inelastic scattering and reduced localization
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The disorder-induced perturbations of the crystal structure, intentionally introduced to our material, likely results in the reduced Landau level separation and significant overlap between adjacent levels. Consequently, we may also deal with inelastic scattering (apart from elastic) and hence the reduced electron localization as compared with pure materials.

mechanism_principle.content: Because Fermi pockets are pinned to L points, rotating the field scans the Fermi-surface cross-sections of a pocket
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since Fermi surface pockets are ”pinned” to the ”L” points, therefore they align with the four < 111 > directions. Assuming this and the fact that we align the field with the principal axes of the Fermi surface cross-section, therefore by changing the angle θ between the magnetic field and one of the (111) crystallographic planes we can ”scan” the Fermi surface cross-sections of one Fermi pocket.

mechanism_principle.content: The local curvature of frequency-versus-angle distinguishes maximum from minimum cross-sections and matches the Maslov-index sign
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The tangent shape of this function reflects the sensitivity of the extreme orbits to the field rotation and the second derivative d2F/dθ2 describes their curvature. The sign of the second derivative is equivalent to the sign of the Maslov index, i.e. denotes whether the maximum or minimum cross section of the Fermi surface is probed.

mechanism_principle.content: These transport effects are attributed to nontrivial Berry curvature and Berry monopoles near Weyl points
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: These effects are believed to originate from the nontrivial Berry curvature and the Berry monopoles near the Weyl points, providing an intrinsic contribution to their emergence.

mechanism_principle.content: Chemical alloy disorder makes zero-gap band inversion sequential and valley-discriminating
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In the presence of chemical (electronic) alloy disorder the band inversion at zero-gap state takes place sequentially, discriminating the four electron valleys.

mechanism_principle.content: A field-independent intrinsic anomalous Hall effect is taken to signify finite 3D Berry curvature and thus a 3D Weyl semimetal phase.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The emergence of such a contribution, independent of external magnetic field, was treated as an initial indication of a finite three-dimensional Berry curvature and, consequently, of the realization of a 3D WSM phase in the investigated samples.

mechanism_principle.content: Quadratic scaling of second-harmonic Hall voltage with current is treated as the signature of the quantum nonlinear Hall effect.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: A quadratic scaling of the second-harmonic transverse voltage with the applied current was analyzed as a characteristic signature of the quantum nonlinear Hall effect.

mechanism_principle.content: Electronic band structure is strongly governed by the spatial distribution of Sn atoms in the supercell.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the electronic band structure strongly depends on the spatial distribution of Sn atoms in the supercell.

mechanism_principle.content: Anomalous Hall conductivity is linked to Berry curvature averaged over occupied states/Fermi surface.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: σAHE is related to the Berry curvature (Ωz) via the equation

mechanism_principle.content: The dominant mechanism is attributed to intrinsic anomalous Hall effect from large Berry curvature generated by inversion-symmetry breaking.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: We assign this dominating mechanism to IAHE associated with large Berry curvature arising when the system undergoes inversion symmetry breakdown.

mechanism_principle.content: The A-B/A-A-S interpretation is supported because insulating Cr-Te nanoprecipitates provide loop sizes matching the oscillation-derived area.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Our con- clusions are supported by the existence of the insulating nanoprecipitates based on Cr-Te compounds in our samples. The surface area calculated basing on the frequencies of the A-B and A-A-S oscillations is comparable with the dimensions of these inclusions and yields 100 nm2.

hypothesis_statement.content: The proposed approach should create favorable conditions for realizing the Weyl semimetal phase in tunable complex IV-VI compounds.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Consequently, the proposed approach creates favorable conditions for realizing the Weyl semimetal phase not just for one material with one specific composition, but in tunable complex IV-VI compounds.

hypothesis_statement.content: Small anisotropy may indicate the Fermi level lies near the Weyl-node touching points
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Small anisotropy may, in our case, provide additional evidence that the Fermi level crosses the Fermi surface in the vicinity of the Weyl node touching points.

hypothesis_statement.content: Field-periodic oscillations above the quantum limit may come from Aharonov-Bohm and Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak interference
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: One possible interpretation is that they correspond to the Aharonov-Bohm and Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak oscillations and originate from the quantum interference effects of charge carriers.

hypothesis_statement.content: Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr with 0.25<x<0.45 is proposed as a new Weyl semimetal arising from alloy disorder and sequential band inversion
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr substitutional alloy with Sn content in the window 0.25 < x < 0.45 constitute new intriguing Weyl semimetal system originating from the influence of the chemical alloy disorder on the multivalley electronic structure of this semiconductor, resulting in the sequential band inversions at zero energy gap in various valleys.

hypothesis_statement.content: Transport measurements were designed to test for a Berry phase and the emergence of a 3D Weyl semimetal phase in Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Electrical transport measurements were conducted to examine the existence of a Berry phase and to establish the emergence of a three-dimensional Weyl semimetal (3D WSM) phase in Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr (0 ≤x ≤1) crystals.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors test the expectation of single-carrier conductivity in their samples.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To support the hypothesis of single-carrier conductivity in our samples we have also at- tempted to fit a two-band conduction model to our ρxx(B) and ρyx(B) data.

evidence_result.content: The study observes emergence of a 3D Weyl semimetal phase for Sn compositions 0.25 < x < 0.45.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We observe the emergence of the three dimensional (3D) Weyl semimetal phase over a range of Sn compositions, namely for 0.25 < x < 0.45.

evidence_result.content: Magnetotransport data support the Weyl semimetal interpretation and the link between Berry curvature magnitude and electrical properties.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We provide magnetotransport evidence for this and verify the relationship between the magnitude of the experimentally determined Berry curvature and the electrical properties of these materials.

evidence_result.content: Thermal conductivity measurements independently confirm the quantum transport regime seen in magnetoresistance.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Quantum transport regime observed in magnetoresistance is also independently confirmed by ther- mal conductivity measurements.

evidence_result.content: One sample shows room-temperature re-entrance of the chiral anomaly, in addition to a 93–150 K occurrence.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For one of our samples we observe the striking phenomenon of the room-temperature re-entrance of the chiral anomaly, in addition to its occurrence in the 93–150 K temperature range.

evidence_result.content: A pronounced chiral-anomaly-induced negative magnetoresistance up to 75% is observed.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We also note a pronounced chiral anomaly-induced negative magnetoresis- tance, reaching up to 75%.

evidence_result.content: Negative longitudinal magnetoresistance is treated as an experimental signature of chiral anomaly and 3D Weyl semimetal phase.
evidence_result.evidence_span: It is reflected experimentally as negative magnetoresistance (MR∥) and observation of chiral anomaly is treated as one of the crucial signatures confirming presence of the 3D Weyl semimetal phase.

evidence_result.content: Samples with 0.25 < x < 0.45 show a sudden drop in carrier concentration and Fermi energy.
evidence_result.evidence_span: for samples with Sn contents in the intermediate composition range: 0.25 < x < 0.45, we observe highly unusual transport properties - sudden drop of carrier concentration and Fermi energy.

evidence_result.content: High-field magnetotransport confirms a Berry-curvature-induced Weyl semimetal phase in the system.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Subsequent high field magneto-transport measurements of the resistivity tensor confirm that our system realizes the Berry curvature induced Weyl semimetal phase.

evidence_result.content: Intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in perpendicular field and chiral anomaly under parallel electric and magnetic fields support the Weyl semimetal phase.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Especially, this is evidenced by the observations of the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in perpendicular magnetic field and chiral anomaly in parallel electric and magnetic fields.

evidence_result.content: Quantum nonlinear Hall effect and second-harmonic detection confirm the Weyl semimetal phase.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Also, the studies of the quantum nonlinear Hall effect and the detection of the second harmonic signal do confirm the existence of the Weyl semimetal phase in the investigated system.

evidence_result.content: Shubnikov-de-Haas oscillations provide evidence for a π Berry phase in the samples.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Additionally, quantum transport and especially the Shubnikov-de-Haas oscillations, detected in several of our samples, due to the good crystal quality, provided crucial evidence for the π Berry phase in the studied samples.

evidence_result.content: QNHE data indicate a Berry-curvature dipole via quadratic second-harmonic response
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure 5E presents the results of the QNHE implying the presence of the Berry curvature dipole, reflected by the quadratic dependence of the second harmonic to the AC current excitation33,48.

evidence_result.content: QNHE is strongest in TCI, much smaller in WSM, and nearly vanishes in region III
evidence_result.evidence_span: As can be seen, the most prominent signal is characteristic for TCI and in the WSM phase the signal is almost one order of magnitude smaller, however, all is within hundreds of nanovolts. In the region (III), i.e. where the trivial charge carriers dominate the QNHE almost completely vanishes.

evidence_result.content: Below 50 K zero-field resistivity rises sharply, signaling disappearance of the 3D WSM phase
evidence_result.evidence_span: Below 50 K a sharp increase in ρ0 is observed, indicating disappearance of the 3D WSM phase.

evidence_result.content: Absence of chiral anomaly, IAHE, and strong reduction in Fz at low temperatures supports loss of the 3D WSM phase
evidence_result.evidence_span: This interpretation is supported by the absence of other signatures of a 3D WSM, such as the chiral anomaly and the IAHE, accompanied by a drastic reduction in Fz at these temperatures.

evidence_result.content: Negative longitudinal resistivity contribution disappears by about 40 degrees and only positive MR remains at larger angles
evidence_result.evidence_span: We observe that it vanishes already at small angles θ ∼40◦(Fig. 6). As the angle increases only the positive MR is present.

evidence_result.content: Angular dependence confirms the chiral-anomaly scenario
evidence_result.evidence_span: Since the negative magnetoresistance is most pronounced when the electric and magnetic fields are parallel, the presented results confirm the chiral anomaly-scenario.

evidence_result.content: AC and DC magnetotransport give the same results, supporting intrinsic origin of the effect
evidence_result.evidence_span: Additionally, for several samples we conduct magneto-transport measurements using the DC and AC techniques and we obtain the same results in both these approaches.

evidence_result.content: Additional tests support chiral anomaly as the origin of the observed effects
evidence_result.evidence_span: All these efforts provide the evidence that chiral anomaly is the origin of the observed effects and the details of these studies are included in Supplementary Notes S.V - S.VII.

evidence_result.content: Quantum oscillations observed over a wide temperature range indicate good crystalline quality
evidence_result.evidence_span: During magneto-transport measurements, the quantum oscillations were observed for several of our samples, in a wide temperature range (Fig. 3B, D, F), providing evidence for good crystalline quality of these samples.

evidence_result.content: Only a single oscillation frequency is observed, likely from 3D WSM states
evidence_result.evidence_span: We observe only a single oscillation frequency, most likely arising from the three-dimensional WSM states.

evidence_result.content: Small cyclotron effective mass is measured
evidence_result.evidence_span: The obtained value of the cyclotron effective mass m∗from fitting the thermal damping term is (0.029+/-0.003) m0 (Fig. 7C).

evidence_result.content: Landau-level analysis deviates from trivial expectations, supporting nontrivial topology
evidence_result.evidence_span: For sample II (x=0.26) the obtained values deviate from those expected for trivial systems, supporting the presence of nontrivial band topology.

evidence_result.content: Measured Maslov indices are consistent with a 3D Weyl semimetal
evidence_result.evidence_span: The obtained Maslov indexes δ are: 0.130 and -0.125 for B ⊥E (Fig. 8A) and B ∥E (Fig. 8B), respectively, assuming the Berry phase exactly equals π and the whole experimental error is included in δ. This confirms that our system is a 3D Weyl semimetal.

evidence_result.content: Hall and SdH carrier densities differ from the expected ratio, indicating ferroelectric distortion in one L valley
evidence_result.evidence_span: The calculated carrier density nSdH is 1.1 x 1017 cm−3, while the Hall carrier density nH is 7 x 1017 cm−3, which gives the ratio nH / nSdH ≈6, instead of 8 (4 L-valleys x 2 = 8 Weyl cones), pointing to the ferroelectric distortion in one of the four ”L” valleys, which is in agreement with the literature3,48.

evidence_result.content: Full Lifshitz-Kosevich fit agrees well with SdH data
evidence_result.evidence_span: Using previously determined values allows us to obtain a very good fit, as depicted in Fig. 9A.

evidence_result.content: The same parameters also fit thermal conductivity qualitatively well
evidence_result.evidence_span: The fit shows good qualitative agreement with the experimental data (Fig. 9B).

evidence_result.content: Angle-dependent measurements on another sample confirm oscillation frequencies and Maslov-index signs
evidence_result.evidence_span: We implement this procedure for sample III (x=0.27), thereby confirming the oscillation frequencies and the sign of the Maslov indexes, obtained for sample II (Fig. 8).

evidence_result.content: Frequency ratio indicates a nearly spherical Fermi surface with only slight anisotropy
evidence_result.evidence_span: The frequencies Frqmax = 6.8 T and Frqmin = 5.2 T were obtained for the cross-sections Amax and Amin, respectively. The ratio Frqmax/Frqmin ∝Amax/Amin ∝6.8/5.2 ∝1.3 ± 0.2 indicates a nearly spherical shape of the Fermi surface and only slight anisotropy, being in agreement with Ref.3.

evidence_result.content: Theoretical and experimental Fermi-surface cross-section ratios are in good agreement
evidence_result.evidence_span: We obtain A(11¯2)/A(111) = 1.1 ± 0.1, which is in good agreement with the ratio of the extreme frequencies Frq[11¯2]/Frq[111] = 6.8/5.2 = 1.3 ± 0.2.

evidence_result.content: DFT supports experimentally inferred Weyl points and Fermi-surface geometry over a broad composition range
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our transport measurements findings (existence of the Weyl points in a broad temperature and crystal composition range and particular geometry of the Fermi surface cross-sections and their angular dependence) got support in the theoretical calculations based on Density Functional Theory.

evidence_result.content: Theory confirms the WSM composition window close to experiment
evidence_result.evidence_span: As shown in Fig. 11, our theoretical calculations confirm the experimentally determined Sn composition range in which the WSM phase is present with sufficient accuracy: Weyl points with zero energy-gap are observed for Sn compositions in the range 0.28 ≤x ≤0.44 for comparison with the experimental Sn composition range: 0.25 ≤x ≤0.45.

evidence_result.content: Magnetotransport supports the theoretically identified Weyl-node pairs
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our magnetotransport experiments support our theoretical calculations that identified the pairs of Weyl nodes with topological charges.

evidence_result.content: The alloys show nonlinear quantum Hall effect, intrinsic anomalous Hall effect, and chiral anomaly
evidence_result.evidence_span: Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr alloys exhibit several peculiar magneto-transport phenomena: including the nonlinear quantum Hall effect, the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect and the chiral anomaly under parallel electric and magnetic fields.

evidence_result.content: The study demonstrates magnetotransport evidence for a 3D Weyl semimetal phase and links Berry curvature magnitude to electrical properties
evidence_result.evidence_span: In this study, we demonstrate magnetotransport evidence for the presence of the 3D Weyl semimetal phase in Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr bulk crystals and verify the relationship between the magnitude of the determined Berry curvature and the electrical properties of these materials.

evidence_result.content: A consistent description of chiral anomaly is obtained using experimentally estimated average Berry curvature and its temperature/composition dependence
evidence_result.evidence_span: We obtain a consistent description of the chiral anomaly in terms of experimentally estimated average Berry curvature and its temperature and composition dependencies.

evidence_result.content: In some samples chiral anomaly persists over most of the temperature range and can re-enter near room temperature
evidence_result.evidence_span: For several samples chiral anomaly covers almost the entire temperature range. Moreover, for one of our samples, we observe the striking phenomenon of the room temperature re-entrance of the chiral anomaly, in addition to its presence in the 93–150 K temperature range.

evidence_result.content: Finite SdH frequency at 90 degrees rules out a 2D electron gas origin
evidence_result.evidence_span: The finite oscillation frequency observed at an angle of 90 degrees, provides direct evidence that the oscillations do not originate from a 2D electron gas, since in that case, no oscillations would be expected for the B ∥E configuration.

evidence_result.content: Angular SdH dependence plus π Berry phase confirm 3D topological WSM states
evidence_result.evidence_span: Thus, the angular dependence of the SdH frequency, together with the π Berry phase extracted from the Landau level index plot, confirms the 3D origin of the electronic states and points to a topological WSM phase.

evidence_result.content: Maslov index of 1/8 provides additional evidence for 3D Fermi-surface character
evidence_result.evidence_span: Moreover, additional evidence for the 3D character of the Fermi surface, is provided by the Maslov index of 1/8, extracted from the SdH oscillations with high accuracy.

evidence_result.content: Berry-curvature-related magnetotransport strongly supports the Weyl semimetal phase in Pb1−xSnxTe:Cr
evidence_result.evidence_span: In conclusion, we believe that our experimental observations and analysis of variety of magnetotransport effects with the Berry curvature contributions to both resistivity and Hall effect, strongly support the presence of the Weyl semimetal phase in Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr.

evidence_result.content: Previous magnetic measurements indicate the host is paramagnetic and contains ferromagnetic Cr-Te nanoinclusions in the matrix.
evidence_result.evidence_span: our magnetic measurements, including SQUID magnetometry and Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR), performed during previous studies42,51,76,77 indicate that host material is paramagnetic and contains various ferromagnetic Cr-Te nanoinclusions embedded in the Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr matrix.

evidence_result.content: Carrier concentrations from two voltage-contact pairs differed by less than 5%, indicating homogeneous crystals.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the small discrepancy of the results collected from both pairs (less than 5% difference in the determined values of carrier concentration) indicates a high degree of homogeneity in the grown crystals

evidence_result.content: Shubnikov-de Haas analysis yielded effective mass, Dingle temperature, relaxation time, and extreme Fermi-surface cross-sections.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The analysis provided the important material parameters, such as effective mass, Dingle temperature and relaxation time. Moreover, the oscillation frequencies obtained in both measurement configurations allowed the determination of the extreme Fermi surface cross-sections.

evidence_result.content: Berry curvature versus temperature was obtained for representative samples in the Weyl-semimetal regime.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure S1 shows the averaged Berry curvature Fz as a function of temperature for several representative Pb1−xSnxCryTe samples (0.26≤x≤0.42, 0.01≤y≤0.02), i.e. from the WSM regime.

evidence_result.content: The fitting formula describes the parallel-field conductivity data well.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As can be seen from Fig. S3 we achieved a very good description of the experimental data.

evidence_result.content: Similar chiral-anomaly signals on three contact pairs show current jetting is absent.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The signal measured on three pairs of contacts simultaneously exhibited similar response with the chiral anomaly on each pair, revealing the absence of current jetting.

evidence_result.content: DC and AC measurements give identical results.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The results obtained using both techniques are identical

constraint.content: The material system is studied across the full tin composition range from x = 0 to x = 1, covering both topological crystalline insulator and trivial regimes.
constraint.evidence_span: covering the full range of tin (0 ≤x ≤1), i.e. spanning both the topological crys- talline insulator and trivial electronic regimes

constraint.content: Fermi-arc SdH oscillations are expected only in ultrathin samples of a few nanometers with weak scattering
constraint.evidence_span: According to the literature71–73, SdH oscillations associated with two-dimensional fermions residing on Fermi arcs are expected to be observable only in samples with extremely small thicknesses, of the order of a few nanometers, where scattering effects remain sufficiently weak.

constraint.content: Current experimental methods cannot directly observe the closely spaced Weyl points
constraint.evidence_span: However, due to small distances between two Weyl points their experimental observation (e.g. Angular-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy) is impossible at present.

constraint.content: Because of strong segregation, the studied samples are expected to have Cr up to 0.5 at.% of cations.
constraint.evidence_span: However, we note that, due to strong segrega- tion, the studied samples are expected to exhibit the regime where Cr constitutes up to 0.5 at.% of the cations.

constraint.content: The very small k-space separation of Weyl points prevents experimental observation of Fermi arcs by ARPES.
constraint.evidence_span: the separation of the Weyl points in k-space is very small, thus it is impossible to observe experimentally Fermi arcs in the Angular Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy experiments.

constraint.content: To interpret Shubnikov-de Haas data, Fermi-surface cross-section areas are required.
constraint.evidence_span: Interpretation of Shubnikov-de Haas measurements requires knowledge of Fermi surface cross section areas.

constraint.content: Berry-curvature extraction assumes the intrinsic anomalous Hall contribution does not depend on magnetic field.
constraint.evidence_span: We assume that the intrinsic contribution is constant in the magnetic field.

contradiction.content: Measured Fermi-surface anisotropy is far smaller than expected for parent PbTe and SnTe
contradiction.evidence_span: We determine an anisotropy factor of 1.3 ± 0.2, in contrast to the much larger values of 2.4-3.2, expected for the ellipsoidal Fermi surfaces shape of parent PbTe, SnTe compounds.

contradiction.content: Measured transport strongly disagrees with the simulated two-carrier model.
contradiction.evidence_span: In contrast to the simulated ρxx using the two-carrier model along with the carrier concentration and mobility extracted from the Hall resistivity curves, the measured ρxx and ρyx data are far deviated from the two-carrier model.

problem_motivation.content: Identifying a true Weyl/chiral-anomaly signal is challenging: supercell calculations often yield trivial positive or negative gaps instead of a Weyl-point-containing configuration, and even when negative magnetoresistance is observed it can be mistaken for weak localization rather than chiral anomaly.
evidence_spans: Since chiral anomaly is not easy to identify and may be confused with the weak localization, long established in the literature8, we perform additional tests to verify these mechanisms.
Usually we obtain results with positive or negative energy gaps. That is why finding the system containing Weyl points is not an easy task.

prior_approach.content: Conventional prior treatment of Pb1−xSnx-based alloys used the virtual crystal approximation (VCA), assuming a composition-driven transition directly from trivial to topological phases.
evidence_spans: According to the classical convention, these materials are usually considered within the virtual crystal approximation (VCA), where, for a given composition, the transition from trivial to topological phase occurs.

prior_approach.content: Prior theory and alloy-disorder studies proposed that chemical disorder can drive sequential band inversions in multiple valleys and produce an intermediate/extended nontrivial Weyl-semimetal-like regime with the Fermi level near Weyl nodes. This includes Wang et al. on Pb1−xSnxSe, Lusakowski et al. on Pb1−xSnxTe, and theory identifying Weyl nodes by DFT.
evidence_spans: We experimentally verify the theoretically pre- dicted role of chemical disorder in this multivalley electron system, which leads to sequential band inversions in various valleys and places the Fermi level close to the pairs of Weyl nodes, as identified in the density functional theory calculations.
Wang et al.13 demonstrated that chemical disorder on cation position in Pb1–xSnxSe alloys can induce an intermediate WSM phase during the sequential band inversion in four ”L” valleys.

Similar conclusion was reached earlier by Lusakowski et al.12 in the study on Pb1–xSnxTe alloys. In particular, the work shows how alloy disorder broadens the transition region between trivial and topological phases, producing an extended transition regime associated with nontrivial topology.

prior_approach.content: Liang et al. previously showed that pressure in Pb1−xSnxTe:In can drive a transition from a topological crystalline insulator to a topological metallic phase associated with Weyl nodes.
evidence_spans: For instance Liang et al. demonstrate that applying pressure to Pb1–xSnxTe:In, material undergoes a pressure-driven transition from TCI to a topological metallic phase associated with Weyl nodes.

prior_approach.content: Earlier work established negative longitudinal magnetoresistance in parallel electric and magnetic fields as a common transport signature associated with the chiral anomaly in Weyl/Dirac systems, first reported in Bi1−xSbx and later in materials such as Cd3As2, NaBi3, TaAs, TaP, and α-Sn.
evidence_spans: Chiral anomaly-induced negative MR∥has been observed for the first time in Bi1–xSbx, x = 0.03 in 201319. Soon after, researchers also reported its presence for Dirac and Weyl semimetals such as: Cd3As222,23 , NaBi324 , TaAs6,25,26, TaP28, α-Sn29 .
This geometry was chosen to measure negative magnetoresistance, commonly associated with the chiral anomaly in Weyl semimetals.

prior_approach.content: Prior magnetotransport models used Argyres and Adams for longitudinal magnetoresistance (including possible negative MR∥) and Abrikosov’s quantum magnetoresistance model for non-saturating linear transverse magnetoresistance.
evidence_spans: These findings were made independently by two research groups - the model of Argyres and Adams6,30 addresses longitudinal magnetoresistance and may lead to negative MR∥, whereas second model of quantum magnetoresistance, implemented by Abrikosov31,32, predicts a non-saturating linear MR⊥.

prior_approach.content: A Princeton group previously observed a nonlinear Hall contribution in Pb1−xSnxTe and attributed it to large Berry curvature near Weyl nodes.
evidence_spans: A few years later3 the scientific group from Princeton observed a nonlinear Hall contribution (σyx) beyond the ordinary linear Hall effect in Pb1–xSnxTe, which they assigned to the large Berry curvature situated near the Weyl nodes.

prior_approach.content: The authors’ prior work on Pb1−xSnxTe:Cr mapped band inversion, band offsets, and the Cr resonant level across the full composition range, and earlier publications also reported crystal characterization (SEM, EDX, XRD, SIMS, EDXF) and magnetic measurements (SQUID, EPR).
evidence_spans: Our recent studies were devoted to the band inversion and band-offsets in Cr-doped Pb1–xSnxTe bulk crystals covering whole range of Sn composition (0 ≤x ≤1)42. In that study we also determine the position of the Cr resonant level over the entire Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr phase diagram (0 ≤x ≤1).

All the details regarding characterization of the obtained crys- tals, including chemical composition, morphology and crystal structure - namely scanning electron microscopy (SEM) together with the energy dispersive X-ray spectrometry (EDX), X-ray diffraction (XRD), secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) and energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (EDXF) - have been reported in our previous publications42,76.
Also our magnetic measurements, including SQUID magnetometry and Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR), performed during previous studies42,51,76,77

prior_approach.content: The computational methodology built on prior work: earlier references discussed the need to reduce Pb 6p spin-orbit strength in DFT, and the method for locating Weyl points was adopted from a previous reference.
evidence_spans: The necessity of such reduction was previously discussed in Ref. 80.
The method of finding the Weyl points was described in Ref. 47.

prior_approach.content: Prior analyses used a standard fitting form for magnetoconductivity combining a chiral-anomaly B^2 term with a 3D weak-antilocalization quantum-interference term.
evidence_spans: The above formula consists of two contributions: (i) chiral anomaly propor- tional to B2 term4 and (ii) quantum interference term in the form of the weak antilocalization for the 3D WSM system5,6.

prior_approach.content: An alternative prior interpretation explained magnetic-field-periodic oscillations as arising from pseudospin Landau levels in the ultra-quantum limit.
evidence_spans: There is also another alternative, considering oscillations periodic in the magnetic field, attributed to pseudospin Landau levels in the regime of ultra quantum limit10,11.

prior_limitation.content: Prior use of the Fermi-level pinning effect had been limited solely to improving thermoelectric performance.
evidence_spans: whose application has so far been limited solely to improving thermoelectric performance43–46.

rejected_alternative.content: The standard VCA picture with a single band-inversion point at x = 0.35 in Pb1−xSnxTe is rejected in favor of a compositional-disorder-driven transition through a WSM phase.
evidence_spans: This behavior may be understood in terms of compositional-disorder driven transition to WSM phase according to earlier theoretical predictions12,13,47, instead of the VCA approach with band inversion point situated at x = 0.35 in Pb1–xSnxTe.

rejected_alternative.content: Magnetic-origin giant/colossal magnetoresistance is rejected as the cause of the observed effect because it would be expected in both perpendicular and parallel MR geometries, unlike the angle-selective behavior seen here.
evidence_spans: Otherwise, if the observed effect were due to giant or colossal MR of magnetic origin, reported in literature62–64 it should occur in both perpendicular and parallel MR configurations.

rejected_alternative.content: Current-jetting/geometry-size effects are excluded as the source of the negative magnetoresistance.
evidence_spans: We also exclude the geometry and size effects, the so called current-jetting, which can result in negative magneto-resistance, but is associated mainly with inhomogeneities of the electric field distribution6,59,65.

rejected_alternative.content: Alternative explanations for the linear magnetoresistance other than Abrikosov’s quantum limit are ruled out, including the Parish-Littlewood two-component inhomogeneous-conduction scenario, because Cr-Te inclusions are scarce, do not contribute to conduction, and the samples are compositionally homogeneous.
evidence_spans: Moreover, we rule out the hypotheses regarding the origin of the linear MR in our samples arising from other reasons than Abrikosov’s quantum limit31,32, mentioned in the Introduction57.

In particular we exclude the conduction through two-component inhomogeneous system, such as PbSe matrix with embedded Ag metallic precipitates - the so called Parish-Littlewood model66,67. As mentioned, the presence of Cr-Te nanoinclusions in our samples is very low and does not contribute to conduction. High compositional homogeneity of our samples is confirmed by the SEM/EDX measurements42. It is also confirmed by very similar resistivities obtained for both pairs of contacts. In this regard, we do not have a system containing multiple precipitates differing significantly in resistance that could affect the results.

rejected_alternative.content: A Fermi-arc origin of the oscillations is rejected because the samples are far too thick and no corresponding signatures are observed beyond effects attributed to the chiral anomaly.
evidence_spans: In contrast, thicknesses of our samples are approximately 0.5-1 mm, meaning several orders of magnitude larger. Therefore, based on our data, we do not observe any signatures of Fermi arcs beyond the effects attributed to the chiral anomaly.

rejected_alternative.content: A 2D electron-gas origin of the oscillations is rejected because a finite oscillation frequency persists at 90°, whereas no oscillations would be expected for B ∥ E in a 2D system.
evidence_spans: The finite oscillation frequency observed at an angle of 90 degrees, provides direct evidence that the oscillations do not originate from a 2D electron gas, since in that case, no oscillations would be expected for the B ∥E configuration.

rejected_alternative.content: Using larger supercells as an alternative computational approach was considered but rejected as impractical because the calculations would be too time-consuming.
evidence_spans: Probably the problem would be partially solved by considering larger supercells, but the calculations are long-lasting and this approach is impractical.

rejected_alternative.content: The pseudospin-Landau-level explanation is rejected in favor of the simpler Aharonov-Bohm/Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak interpretation.
evidence_spans: However, we exclude this scenario and adopt the simpler A-B and A-A-S interpretation.

causal_claim.content: Chemical disorder breaks local crystal symmetries and lifts valley degeneracy, causing sequential band inversions in different valleys and placing the Fermi level close to pairs of Weyl nodes.
evidence_spans: chemical disorder in this multivalley electron system, which leads to sequential band inversions in various valleys and places the Fermi level close to the pairs of Weyl nodes

Introducing chemical disorder and other effects, that break local crystal symmetries and split valley degeneracy at high symmetry points of the Brillouin zone (BZ) may lead to significant changes, e.g. in the band inversion process in comparison with TIs/TCIs.

causal_claim.content: Doping with mixed-valence Cr resonant impurities enables tuning of carrier concentration via dopant resonant states.
evidence_spans: Doping with mixed-valence Cr resonant impurities enables exploitation of the unique properties of dopant resonant states, which provide an effective means of tuning carrier concentration.

causal_claim.content: The combination of chemical disorder and Cr resonant-donor doping pins the Fermi level near the nodal touching points/zero-gap state over a wide composition range, enabling strong topological transport contributions and allowing determination of the Cr resonant level over the full phase diagram.
evidence_spans: The combination of these two effects results in the pinning of the Fermi level in the vicinity of the nodal touching points across a wide range of composition.
To investigate these effects, we achieve pinning of the Fermi level in the vicinity of the nodal touching points in Pb1–xSnxTe over a wide range of Sn compositions by doping crystals with Cr.

To reach the physical regime with the sizeable topological contributions to electron transport we successfully applied doping with the resonant donor centre of Cr pinning the Fermi level close to zero-gap state.
This is possible due to the Fermi level pinning effect

causal_claim.content: Breaking time-reversal or inversion symmetry can drive materials into Weyl semimetal states through band inversion during a topological phase transition.
evidence_spans: As a consequence of this symmetry breaking, these materials may evolve into Weyl semimetals through band inversion processes.

causal_claim.content: Applying pressure splits a degenerate Dirac cone into two nondegenerate Weyl cones of opposite chirality separated in momentum space.
evidence_spans: This results in splitting one degenerate Dirac cone where opposite-chirality fermions overlap into two nondegenerate Weyl cones of opposite chiralities separated in momentum space.

causal_claim.content: Closing the bulk gap removes the Dirac mass term, converting the system to a massless Weyl equation with linear dispersion near the Weyl nodes.
evidence_spans: The main highlight of this work in our context is that since a bulk energy-gap, responsible for the mass-term of the Dirac equation is closed in WSMs this may be converted into a massless Weyl equation which results in linear energy dispersion in the vicinity of the two Weyl nodes16,17.

causal_claim.content: Spin-momentum locking suppresses spin-independent backscattering, leading to large non-saturating magnetoresistance and very high mobility.
evidence_spans: electrons in WSMs have spin locked to the momentum, and thus do not undergo back-scattering by spin-independent processes... As a result, they behave like massles relativistic Dirac fermions, giving rise to large non-saturated magnetoresistance, and hence very high mobilities

causal_claim.content: The nontrivial nature of Weyl fermions breaks chiral symmetry, producing the Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly.
evidence_spans: Several decades after Weyl’s achievements, Adler, Bell and Jackiw demonstrated that due to the nontrivial nature of Weyl fermions, the chiral symmetry is no longer preserved, leading to the Adler-Bell-Jackiv anomaly.

causal_claim.content: Applying parallel electric and magnetic fields causes nonconservation of chiral charge between opposite-chirality Weyl nodes.
evidence_spans: Chiral anomaly manifests itself as a non-conservation of chiral charge between two Weyl nodes of opposite chiralities when applying parallel electric and magnetic fields (E ∥B) to the material.

causal_claim.content: Both positive linear transverse magnetoresistance and negative longitudinal magnetoresistance may arise from the system entering the extreme quantum limit, where all electrons occupy only the lowest Landau level.
evidence_spans: Interestingly, both mentioned mechanisms - positive linear, non-saturating MR⊥and negative MR∥, may be the consequence of one and the same phenomenon - both may originate from the system entering the extreme quantum limit, i.e. where all electrons occupy only the lowest Landau level.

causal_claim.content: Berry curvature near Weyl nodes strongly influences longitudinal transport, including the chiral anomaly, and Hall responses.
evidence_spans: The Berry curvature associated with Weyl nodes plays a central role in determining the physical properties of these materials, strongly influencing both: longitudinal charge transport, reflected in the chiral anomaly, and Hall responses.

causal_claim.content: Broken inversion symmetry produces an asymmetric Berry-curvature distribution; together with different occupation of states at k and -k, this leads to a net Berry curvature in the nonlinear quantum Hall effect.
evidence_spans: The resulting asymmetric Berry curvature distribution originates from the broken inversion symmetry under which electrons at momenta k and –k possess opposite Berry curvature.
Hence, charge states for k and -k will be occupied differently leading to the net Berry curvature.

causal_claim.content: Cooling through the trivial-to-WSM transition freezes out trivial bulk carriers and leaves metallic WSM surface-state carriers.
evidence_spans: the resistivity of the sample slowly increases as the temperature is lowered starting from RT, since as the sample undergoes the transition from the trivial to the WSM phase, the trivial bulk carriers are gradually ”frozen out” and the metallic carriers, associated with surface states of 3D WSM remain.

causal_claim.content: Low carrier concentration of TCI surface states causes high zero-field resistivity.
evidence_spans: The zero field resistivity of these states is high since the concentration of the surface-states charge carriers is very low (1016 cm−3).

causal_claim.content: Large perpendicular magnetoresistance hides oscillations unless a second derivative is taken.
evidence_spans: This is a result of a large magnetoresistance MR⊥and to extract the oscillating component a second derivative of the raw data with respect to 1/B should be taken.

causal_claim.content: Disorder suppresses the emergence of distinct, high-amplitude SdH oscillations typical of high-mobility Weyl fermions.
evidence_spans: Although quantum transport effects can still be detected, the disorder prevents the emergence of distinct, high amplitude SdH oscillations that are typically associated with high mobility Weyl fermions.

causal_claim.content: The small amount of Cr-Te nanoinclusions means they do not affect transport.
evidence_spans: Nevertheless, their amount is relatively small and hence they do not affect transport of our samples.

causal_claim.content: Observation of the quantum nonlinear Hall effect provided complementary evidence for nontrivial Berry curvature and supported identification of the Weyl semimetal phase.
evidence_spans: Observation of this effect provided complementary evidence for nontrivial Berry curvature and supported the identification of the Weyl semimetal phase in Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr.

causal_claim.content: Mismatch with the two-carrier model implies that another mechanism dominates magnetotransport.
evidence_spans: This means that a notable mecha- nism dominates the magnetotransport in the current system

causal_claim.content: Small electric/magnetic-field misalignment causes high-field deviation from the theoretical model by adding positive magnetoresistance.
evidence_spans: Deviation of the high-field conductivity from the theoretical model originates from a small admixture of large positive magnetoresistance due to a small misalignment between the electric and magnetic fields.

causal_claim.content: Observation of chiral anomaly in the parallel configuration, together with agreement between DC and AC data, supports interpreting the system as a 3D Weyl semimetal and confirms chiral anomaly as the source of the observed effects while ruling out thermoelectric artifacts.
evidence_spans: The presence of chiral anomaly in the parallel configuration supports the interpretation that our system is a 3D WSM.
The results obtained using both techniques are identical, confirming that the chiral anomaly underlies the observed effects.
It also excludes thermoelectric effects, such as Peltier or Seebeck effect.

causal_claim.content: If the observed effect were due to magnetic giant/colossal magnetoresistance, it should appear in both perpendicular and parallel configurations; since it does not, that mechanism is not the origin here.
evidence_spans: Otherwise, if the observed effect were due to giant or colossal MR of magnetic origin, reported in literature62–64 it should occur in both perpendicular and parallel MR configurations.

causal_claim.content: If a weak-antilocalization to weak-localization crossover were responsible, the effect would appear in both perpendicular and parallel geometries; therefore it is not the origin here.
evidence_spans: Additionally, it is not related to the weak antilocalization – weak localization transition, since if this were the origin of our results, it would be present as well in the parallel and perpendicular configurations.

causal_claim.content: Magnetic-field-periodic oscillations arise from interference of electron wavefunctions around enclosed magnetic flux; Aharonov-Bohm versus Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak paths produce a twofold phase change, yielding h/e versus h/2e flux periods.
evidence_spans: The oscillations periodic in the magnetic field arise due to the interference of the amplitudes of the electron wave function as the electron encircles the closed loop surroounding the magnetic flux.
This gives the twofold change in the phases of the amplitudes of the A-B and A-A-S oscillations. As a result, the flux period θ in the magnetic field equals h/e or h/2e, respectively.

mechanism_principle.content: Chemical/compositional alloy disorder governs the electronic structure and converts an otherwise sharp, concurrent VCA-like zero-gap band inversion into a sequential, valley-discriminating inversion over a finite composition interval; this disorder-driven regime can host Weyl-semimetal-like states instead of a simple band inversion at x = 0.35.
evidence_spans: From physical perspective, both studies describe essentially the same mechanism - disorder transforms a sharp and concurrent (VCA-like) band inversion into a sequential one with the finite composition range where WSM-like states may emerge.

This behavior may be understood in terms of compositional-disorder driven transition to WSM phase according to earlier theoretical predictions12,13,47, instead of the VCA approach with band inversion point situated at x = 0.35 in Pb1–xSnxTe.
In the presence of chemical (electronic) alloy disorder the band inversion at zero-gap state takes place sequentially, discriminating the four electron valleys.
the electronic band structure strongly depends on the spatial distribution of Sn atoms in the supercell.

mechanism_principle.content: The dominant anomalous transport mechanism is intrinsic and tied to Berry curvature/Berry monopoles near Weyl points: a field-independent anomalous Hall effect is taken as evidence of finite 3D Berry curvature and a 3D Weyl-semimetal phase, with anomalous Hall conductivity linked to Berry curvature over occupied states and enhanced by inversion-symmetry breaking.
evidence_spans: These effects are believed to originate from the nontrivial Berry curvature and the Berry monopoles near the Weyl points, providing an intrinsic contribution to their emergence.

The emergence of such a contribution, independent of external magnetic field, was treated as an initial indication of a finite three-dimensional Berry curvature and, consequently, of the realization of a 3D WSM phase in the investigated samples.
σAHE is related to the Berry curvature (Ωz) via the equation
We assign this dominating mechanism to IAHE associated with large Berry curvature arising when the system undergoes inversion symmetry breakdown.

mechanism_principle.content: Small effective mass is interpreted as evidence that carriers occupy linearly dispersing bands near Weyl nodes.
evidence_spans: The relatively small effective mass obtained in this analysis corresponds to carriers occupying linearly dispersing bands near the Weyl nodes.

mechanism_principle.content: Disorder-induced crystal perturbations likely reduce Landau-level separation and increase overlap between adjacent levels, enabling inelastic as well as elastic scattering and thereby reducing electron localization relative to purer materials.
evidence_spans: The disorder-induced perturbations of the crystal structure, intentionally introduced to our material, likely results in the reduced Landau level separation and significant overlap between adjacent levels. Consequently, we may also deal with inelastic scattering (apart from elastic) and hence the reduced electron localization as compared with pure materials.

mechanism_principle.content: Because Fermi pockets are pinned to the L points along the four <111> directions, rotating the magnetic field scans the cross-sections of a given pocket; the curvature of frequency versus angle then identifies whether the probed orbit is a maximum or minimum cross-section via the sign of the second derivative/Maslov index.
evidence_spans: Since Fermi surface pockets are ”pinned” to the ”L” points, therefore they align with the four < 111 > directions. Assuming this and the fact that we align the field with the principal axes of the Fermi surface cross-section, therefore by changing the angle θ between the magnetic field and one of the (111) crystallographic planes we can ”scan” the Fermi surface cross-sections of one Fermi pocket.

The tangent shape of this function reflects the sensitivity of the extreme orbits to the field rotation and the second derivative d2F/dθ2 describes their curvature. The sign of the second derivative is equivalent to the sign of the Maslov index, i.e. denotes whether the maximum or minimum cross section of the Fermi surface is probed.

mechanism_principle.content: Quadratic scaling of the second-harmonic Hall voltage with current is treated as the signature of the quantum nonlinear Hall effect.
evidence_spans: A quadratic scaling of the second-harmonic transverse voltage with the applied current was analyzed as a characteristic signature of the quantum nonlinear Hall effect.

mechanism_principle.content: The Aharonov-Bohm/Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak interpretation is supported by insulating Cr-Te nanoprecipitates whose loop dimensions match the oscillation-derived area.
evidence_spans: Our con- clusions are supported by the existence of the insulating nanoprecipitates based on Cr-Te compounds in our samples. The surface area calculated basing on the frequencies of the A-B and A-A-S oscillations is comparable with the dimensions of these inclusions and yields 100 nm2.

hypothesis_statement.content: Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr with 0.25<x<0.45 is proposed as a new 3D Weyl semimetal, arising from alloy disorder and sequential band inversion; more broadly, the proposed approach should enable realization of the Weyl semimetal phase in tunable complex IV-VI compounds.
evidence_spans: Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr substitutional alloy with Sn content in the window 0.25 < x < 0.45 constitute new intriguing Weyl semimetal system originating from the influence of the chemical alloy disorder on the multivalley electronic structure of this semiconductor, resulting in the sequential band inversions at zero energy gap in various valleys.

Consequently, the proposed approach creates favorable conditions for realizing the Weyl semimetal phase not just for one material with one specific composition, but in tunable complex IV-VI compounds.

hypothesis_statement.content: Small anisotropy may indicate that the Fermi level lies near the Weyl-node touching points.
evidence_spans: Small anisotropy may, in our case, provide additional evidence that the Fermi level crosses the Fermi surface in the vicinity of the Weyl node touching points.

hypothesis_statement.content: Field-periodic oscillations above the quantum limit may originate from Aharonov-Bohm and Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak quantum interference effects.
evidence_spans: One possible interpretation is that they correspond to the Aharonov-Bohm and Altshuler-Aronov-Spivak oscillations and originate from the quantum interference effects of charge carriers.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study tests the hypothesis that Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr exhibits a Berry phase and an emergent 3D Weyl semimetal phase, using transport measurements.
evidence_spans: Electrical transport measurements were conducted to examine the existence of a Berry phase and to establish the emergence of a three-dimensional Weyl semimetal (3D WSM) phase in Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr (0 ≤x ≤1) crystals.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors hypothesize single-carrier conductivity in their samples.
evidence_spans: To support the hypothesis of single-carrier conductivity in our samples we have also at- tempted to fit a two-band conduction model to our ρxx(B) and ρyx(B) data.

evidence_result.content: Pb1−xSnxTe:Cr shows a 3D Weyl semimetal phase over an intermediate Sn-composition window, experimentally observed for about 0.25 < x < 0.45 and supported by theory for 0.28 ≤ x ≤ 0.44.
evidence_spans: We observe the emergence of the three dimensional (3D) Weyl semimetal phase over a range of Sn compositions, namely for 0.25 < x < 0.45.

As shown in Fig. 11, our theoretical calculations confirm the experimentally determined Sn composition range in which the WSM phase is present with sufficient accuracy: Weyl points with zero energy-gap are observed for Sn compositions in the range 0.28 ≤x ≤0.44 for comparison with the experimental Sn composition range: 0.25 ≤x ≤0.45.

evidence_result.content: Magnetotransport provides overall evidence for the 3D Weyl semimetal phase in Pb1−xSnxTe:Cr and links experimentally determined Berry curvature magnitude to electrical/transport properties.
evidence_spans: We provide magnetotransport evidence for this and verify the relationship between the magnitude of the experimentally determined Berry curvature and the electrical properties of these materials.
Subsequent high field magneto-transport measurements of the resistivity tensor confirm that our system realizes the Berry curvature induced Weyl semimetal phase.

In this study, we demonstrate magnetotransport evidence for the presence of the 3D Weyl semimetal phase in Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr bulk crystals and verify the relationship between the magnitude of the determined Berry curvature and the electrical properties of these materials.

In conclusion, we believe that our experimental observations and analysis of variety of magnetotransport effects with the Berry curvature contributions to both resistivity and Hall effect, strongly support the presence of the Weyl semimetal phase in Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr.
