evidence_result.content: Intermediate-composition samples (0.25 < x < 0.45) show unusual transport with a sudden drop in carrier concentration and Fermi energy, consistent with the Weyl-semimetal regime.
evidence_spans: for samples with Sn contents in the intermediate composition range: 0.25 < x < 0.45, we observe highly unusual transport properties - sudden drop of carrier concentration and Fermi energy.

evidence_result.content: Multiple magnetotransport signatures support the Weyl semimetal phase, including intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in perpendicular field, chiral anomaly under parallel electric and magnetic fields, and the quantum nonlinear Hall effect/second-harmonic response.
evidence_spans: Especially, this is evidenced by the observations of the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in perpendicular magnetic field and chiral anomaly in parallel electric and magnetic fields.
Also, the studies of the quantum nonlinear Hall effect and the detection of the second harmonic signal do confirm the existence of the Weyl semimetal phase in the investigated system.

Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr alloys exhibit several peculiar magneto-transport phenomena: including the nonlinear quantum Hall effect, the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect and the chiral anomaly under parallel electric and magnetic fields.

evidence_result.content: QNHE data imply a Berry-curvature dipole through a quadratic second-harmonic response; the signal is strongest in the TCI phase, about an order of magnitude smaller in the WSM phase, and nearly vanishes in the trivial-carrier region.
evidence_spans: Figure 5E presents the results of the QNHE implying the presence of the Berry curvature dipole, reflected by the quadratic dependence of the second harmonic to the AC current excitation33,48.

As can be seen, the most prominent signal is characteristic for TCI and in the WSM phase the signal is almost one order of magnitude smaller, however, all is within hundreds of nanovolts. In the region (III), i.e. where the trivial charge carriers dominate the QNHE almost completely vanishes.

evidence_result.content: A pronounced chiral-anomaly-induced negative longitudinal magnetoresistance is observed, reaching up to 75%, and negative longitudinal MR is treated as a key experimental signature of chiral anomaly and the 3D Weyl semimetal phase.
evidence_spans: We also note a pronounced chiral anomaly-induced negative magnetoresis- tance, reaching up to 75%.
It is reflected experimentally as negative magnetoresistance (MR∥) and observation of chiral anomaly is treated as one of the crucial signatures confirming presence of the 3D Weyl semimetal phase.

evidence_result.content: Chiral anomaly persists over a broad temperature range in several samples, and one sample shows room-temperature re-entrance in addition to a 93–150 K occurrence.
evidence_spans: For one of our samples we observe the striking phenomenon of the room-temperature re-entrance of the chiral anomaly, in addition to its occurrence in the 93–150 K temperature range.

For several samples chiral anomaly covers almost the entire temperature range. Moreover, for one of our samples, we observe the striking phenomenon of the room temperature re-entrance of the chiral anomaly, in addition to its presence in the 93–150 K temperature range.

evidence_result.content: The angular dependence of longitudinal MR supports the chiral-anomaly interpretation: the negative contribution is strongest for parallel electric and magnetic fields, disappears by about 40°, and only positive MR remains at larger angles.
evidence_spans: We observe that it vanishes already at small angles θ ∼40◦(Fig. 6). As the angle increases only the positive MR is present.
Since the negative magnetoresistance is most pronounced when the electric and magnetic fields are parallel, the presented results confirm the chiral anomaly-scenario.

evidence_result.content: Control measurements support an intrinsic chiral-anomaly origin and argue against artifacts: AC and DC magnetotransport results are identical, three contact pairs show similar signals excluding current jetting, and additional tests further support this interpretation.
evidence_spans: Additionally, for several samples we conduct magneto-transport measurements using the DC and AC techniques and we obtain the same results in both these approaches.
All these efforts provide the evidence that chiral anomaly is the origin of the observed effects and the details of these studies are included in Supplementary Notes S.V - S.VII.
The signal measured on three pairs of contacts simultaneously exhibited similar response with the chiral anomaly on each pair, revealing the absence of current jetting.
The results obtained using both techniques are identical

evidence_result.content: A consistent description of the chiral anomaly is obtained in terms of experimentally estimated average Berry curvature and its temperature/composition dependence; Berry-curvature-versus-temperature was extracted for representative WSM-regime samples.
evidence_spans: We obtain a consistent description of the chiral anomaly in terms of experimentally estimated average Berry curvature and its temperature and composition dependencies.
Figure S1 shows the averaged Berry curvature Fz as a function of temperature for several representative Pb1−xSnxCryTe samples (0.26≤x≤0.42, 0.01≤y≤0.02), i.e. from the WSM regime.

evidence_result.content: At low temperatures the 3D WSM phase disappears: below 50 K zero-field resistivity rises sharply, and the loss of chiral anomaly, IAHE, and strong reduction of Fz support this conclusion.
evidence_spans: Below 50 K a sharp increase in ρ0 is observed, indicating disappearance of the 3D WSM phase.
This interpretation is supported by the absence of other signatures of a 3D WSM, such as the chiral anomaly and the IAHE, accompanied by a drastic reduction in Fz at these temperatures.

evidence_result.content: Thermal-conductivity measurements independently confirm the quantum transport regime seen in magnetoresistance, and the same parameters used for SdH analysis also qualitatively fit the thermal-conductivity data.
evidence_spans: Quantum transport regime observed in magnetoresistance is also independently confirmed by ther- mal conductivity measurements.
The fit shows good qualitative agreement with the experimental data (Fig. 9B).

evidence_result.content: Shubnikov–de Haas oscillations observed over a wide temperature range indicate good crystal quality and provide crucial evidence for a π Berry phase.
evidence_spans: Additionally, quantum transport and especially the Shubnikov-de-Haas oscillations, detected in several of our samples, due to the good crystal quality, provided crucial evidence for the π Berry phase in the studied samples.

During magneto-transport measurements, the quantum oscillations were observed for several of our samples, in a wide temperature range (Fig. 3B, D, F), providing evidence for good crystalline quality of these samples.

evidence_result.content: SdH oscillations show a single frequency likely arising from 3D WSM states rather than a 2D electron gas; finite frequency at 90° rules out a 2D origin, and the angular dependence together with the π Berry phase confirms 3D topological WSM states.
evidence_spans: We observe only a single oscillation frequency, most likely arising from the three-dimensional WSM states.

The finite oscillation frequency observed at an angle of 90 degrees, provides direct evidence that the oscillations do not originate from a 2D electron gas, since in that case, no oscillations would be expected for the B ∥E configuration.

Thus, the angular dependence of the SdH frequency, together with the π Berry phase extracted from the Landau level index plot, confirms the 3D origin of the electronic states and points to a topological WSM phase.

evidence_result.content: SdH/Landau-level analysis supports nontrivial 3D Weyl topology: measured phases deviate from trivial expectations, Maslov indices are consistent with a 3D WSM, and a Maslov index of 1/8 further supports 3D Fermi-surface character.
evidence_spans: For sample II (x=0.26) the obtained values deviate from those expected for trivial systems, supporting the presence of nontrivial band topology.

The obtained Maslov indexes δ are: 0.130 and -0.125 for B ⊥E (Fig. 8A) and B ∥E (Fig. 8B), respectively, assuming the Berry phase exactly equals π and the whole experimental error is included in δ. This confirms that our system is a 3D Weyl semimetal.
Moreover, additional evidence for the 3D character of the Fermi surface, is provided by the Maslov index of 1/8, extracted from the SdH oscillations with high accuracy.

evidence_result.content: SdH analysis yields a small cyclotron effective mass (~0.029 ± 0.003 m0) and, more generally, effective mass, Dingle temperature, relaxation time, and extreme Fermi-surface cross-sections.
evidence_spans: The obtained value of the cyclotron effective mass m∗from fitting the thermal damping term is (0.029+/-0.003) m0 (Fig. 7C).

The analysis provided the important material parameters, such as effective mass, Dingle temperature and relaxation time. Moreover, the oscillation frequencies obtained in both measurement configurations allowed the determination of the extreme Fermi surface cross-sections.

evidence_result.content: Hall and SdH carrier densities differ from the expected Weyl-cone count, suggesting ferroelectric distortion in one of the four L valleys.
evidence_spans: The calculated carrier density nSdH is 1.1 x 1017 cm−3, while the Hall carrier density nH is 7 x 1017 cm−3, which gives the ratio nH / nSdH ≈6, instead of 8 (4 L-valleys x 2 = 8 Weyl cones), pointing to the ferroelectric distortion in one of the four ”L” valleys, which is in agreement with the literature3,48.

evidence_result.content: Lifshitz–Kosevich modeling fits the SdH data well.
evidence_spans: Using previously determined values allows us to obtain a very good fit, as depicted in Fig. 9A.

evidence_result.content: Angle-dependent measurements on another sample confirm the oscillation frequencies and Maslov-index signs found previously.
evidence_spans: We implement this procedure for sample III (x=0.27), thereby confirming the oscillation frequencies and the sign of the Maslov indexes, obtained for sample II (Fig. 8).

evidence_result.content: The Fermi surface is nearly spherical with only slight anisotropy, as indicated by the frequency ratio and by agreement between theoretical and experimental cross-section ratios.
evidence_spans: The frequencies Frqmax = 6.8 T and Frqmin = 5.2 T were obtained for the cross-sections Amax and Amin, respectively. The ratio Frqmax/Frqmin ∝Amax/Amin ∝6.8/5.2 ∝1.3 ± 0.2 indicates a nearly spherical shape of the Fermi surface and only slight anisotropy, being in agreement with Ref.3.
We obtain A(11¯2)/A(111) = 1.1 ± 0.1, which is in good agreement with the ratio of the extreme frequencies Frq[11¯2]/Frq[111] = 6.8/5.2 = 1.3 ± 0.2.

evidence_result.content: DFT supports the experimentally inferred Weyl points, Fermi-surface geometry, angular dependence, and broad composition range of the WSM phase; magnetotransport results are consistent with theoretically identified Weyl-node pairs with topological charge.
evidence_spans: Our transport measurements findings (existence of the Weyl points in a broad temperature and crystal composition range and particular geometry of the Fermi surface cross-sections and their angular dependence) got support in the theoretical calculations based on Density Functional Theory.
Our magnetotransport experiments support our theoretical calculations that identified the pairs of Weyl nodes with topological charges.

evidence_result.content: The fitting formula provides a very good description of the parallel-field conductivity data.
evidence_spans: As can be seen from Fig. S3 we achieved a very good description of the experimental data.

evidence_result.content: The crystals are homogeneous, as carrier concentrations from two voltage-contact pairs differ by less than 5%.
evidence_spans: the small discrepancy of the results collected from both pairs (less than 5% difference in the determined values of carrier concentration) indicates a high degree of homogeneity in the grown crystals

evidence_result.content: Previous magnetic measurements indicate a paramagnetic host material containing ferromagnetic Cr–Te nanoinclusions embedded in the Pb1−xSnxTe:Cr matrix.
evidence_spans: our magnetic measurements, including SQUID magnetometry and Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR), performed during previous studies42,51,76,77 indicate that host material is paramagnetic and contains various ferromagnetic Cr-Te nanoinclusions embedded in the Pb1–xSnxTe:Cr matrix.

constraint.content: The material system is studied across the full tin composition range, x = 0 to x = 1, spanning both the topological crystalline insulator and trivial electronic regimes.
evidence_spans: covering the full range of tin (0 ≤x ≤1), i.e. spanning both the topological crys- talline insulator and trivial electronic regimes

constraint.content: Fermi-arc Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations are expected to be observable only in ultrathin samples a few nanometers thick with sufficiently weak scattering.
evidence_spans: According to the literature71–73, SdH oscillations associated with two-dimensional fermions residing on Fermi arcs are expected to be observable only in samples with extremely small thicknesses, of the order of a few nanometers, where scattering effects remain sufficiently weak.

constraint.content: The very small k-space separation between Weyl points currently prevents direct experimental observation by ARPES, including observation of Fermi arcs.
evidence_spans: However, due to small distances between two Weyl points their experimental observation (e.g. Angular-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy) is impossible at present.
the separation of the Weyl points in k-space is very small, thus it is impossible to observe experimentally Fermi arcs in the Angular Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy experiments.

constraint.content: Due to strong segregation, the studied samples are expected to be in a regime where Cr constitutes up to 0.5 at.% of the cations.
evidence_spans: However, we note that, due to strong segrega- tion, the studied samples are expected to exhibit the regime where Cr constitutes up to 0.5 at.% of the cations.

constraint.content: Interpretation of Shubnikov-de Haas measurements requires knowledge of Fermi-surface cross-sectional areas.
evidence_spans: Interpretation of Shubnikov-de Haas measurements requires knowledge of Fermi surface cross section areas.

constraint.content: Berry-curvature extraction assumes that the intrinsic anomalous Hall contribution is independent of magnetic field.
evidence_spans: We assume that the intrinsic contribution is constant in the magnetic field.

contradiction.content: The measured electronic transport/Fermi-surface behavior contradicts expectations from standard models: the Fermi-surface anisotropy is much smaller than expected for parent PbTe/SnTe (1.3 ± 0.2 vs. 2.4–3.2), and the measured ρxx and ρyx strongly deviate from the simulated two-carrier transport model.
evidence_spans: We determine an anisotropy factor of 1.3 ± 0.2, in contrast to the much larger values of 2.4-3.2, expected for the ellipsoidal Fermi surfaces shape of parent PbTe, SnTe compounds.

In contrast to the simulated ρxx using the two-carrier model along with the carrier concentration and mobility extracted from the Hall resistivity curves, the measured ρxx and ρyx data are far deviated from the two-carrier model.
